cards.title: That drawer of old prescriptions? Useful.
cards.body: Old prescriptions feel like clutter. They actually tell a story a new doctor may need. The trick is keeping them in order.

cards.title: Don't throw them away
cards.body: Past prescriptions show what was tried, what dose was given and what caused trouble. Keep them, even after the treatment ended.

cards.title: Sort by person, then by date
cards.body: One file per family member, newest on top, older ones at the back. A quick label with the year helps.

cards.title: Mark what is current
cards.body: Put a sticky note or a tick on the prescription being followed right now. It stops anyone mixing up old and new doses.

cards.title: Never restart old medicines on your own
cards.body: An old prescription is a record, not permission. Before using leftover medicine or repeating an old course, check with the doctor or pharmacist.

cards.title: Photograph and back them up
cards.body: Snap the important ones and save them in a folder per person. Paper fades, and the original may be needed someday.

cards.title: Old paper, real value
cards.body: Keep them, sort them, mark the current one and back up the rest. Your next doctor visit gets a lot easier.

takeaway: Keep old prescriptions sorted by person and date, mark the current one, back them up and never restart old medicines alone.
share: Don't throw away old prescriptions. Sort them, mark the current one, never reuse without asking.
